title: unified-rollouts-add-metric-driven-shadowing-and-auto-rollback-metric-thresholds
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Add metric-driven shadowing and auto-rollback configuration options for unified rollouts; no breaking API changes.
description:
Problem: Customers have asked for an automated way to run shadow traffic against new model variants while monitoring key metrics (latency, error-rate, perplexity/quality score) and automatically trigger rollbacks when regressions exceed configured thresholds. This PR adds support for metric-driven shadowing and an auto-rollback policy to the unified rollouts controller and exposes configuration knobs in the rollout manifest and Console.

Summary of changes: Implemented shadow traffic metric hooks, evaluation windowing, per-metric thresholding, and an auto-rollback controller that monitors rolling metrics and triggers rollback if thresholds are breached for configured consecutive windows. Added new rollout manifest fields (shadow: {enabled, percent, metrics}, autoRollback: {enabled, windows, consecutiveFailures}). Integrated with existing metrics ingestion pipeline and alerting hooks. Updated Console UI text and rollout API docs.

Design notes: The controller evaluates metrics in fixed windows (default 1m) and supports aggregations (p95 latency, error_rate, quality_regression). Each metric has a direction (increase/decrease) and a threshold. The auto-rollback policy requires N consecutive windows breaching thresholds to avoid noisy rollbacks. Shadow traffic is executed as non-intrusive mirroring — responses are not returned to users but are processed by the evaluator. We reuse the existing metrics labels and aggregation keys so customers can plug Prometheus or our internal TSDB endpoints.

Config schema (high level): rollout.spec.shadow.enabled: bool; rollout.spec.shadow.percent: int; rollout.spec.shadow.metrics: list of {name, threshold, direction, aggregator}; rollout.spec.autoRollback.enabled: bool; rollout.spec.autoRollback.windows: int; rollout.spec.autoRollback.consecutiveFailures: int.

Rollout impact: Default behavior is opt-in. No change to existing rollout controllers unless fields are present. The controller is fault-tolerant: metric ingestion failures will mark evaluator state degraded but will not auto-rollback unless explicit flag autoRollback.forceful=true (not enabled by default).

Testing: Unit tests for metric windowing and threshold evaluation; integration test that simulates shadow traffic and verifies auto-rollback triggers after consecutive failures; e2e smoke tests with canary->primary transition to ensure no regression in steady-state. Performance: added light-weight sampling for shadow traffic to bound overhead; measured <1% CPU increase on controller for 1k rps of rollout events in benchmark lab.

Migration plan: Console and CLI will accept new fields gracefully. Recommend customers start with conservative thresholds (e.g., p95 latency +20%, error_rate +0.5%) and low shadow percent.

Related work: builds on ENG-2241 (rollout observability) and ENG-2273 (rollout API v2). Addresses SUP-412 support case from customer X.

- [x] Unit and integration tests
